name: Sorrow-Glacial
geological_features: Continent-spanning glaciers moving at visible rates
Subsurface liquid water ocean maintained by tidal heating
Ice geysers erupting saline water hundreds of meters high
specific_features: Frozen remains of an alien vessel embedded in the northern ice sheet, partially excavated
description: Sorrow-Glacial is a medium-sized ice world encased in glaciers that move with visible, inexorable purpose, grinding across the surface at rates measured in meters per day rather than the centimeters typical of such formations. Beneath the ice shell lies a liquid water ocean kept warm by tidal interaction with a nearby gas giant, and saline geysers punch through weak points in the crust to spray plumes of water that freeze into glittering towers on the surface.

The thin atmosphere carries the crack and groan of shifting ice at all hours, a soundscape of compression and fracture that early explorers compared to the weeping of something vast and inconsolable. The cold is absolute and penetrating, the kind that finds every gap in thermal protection and punishes it.

Embedded in the northern ice sheet lies the frozen remains of an alien vessel, its hull material unlike anything in material science databases. Partial excavation has revealed interior spaces designed for beings of non-humanoid anatomy, and the cargo holds contain sealed containers whose contents register as biologically active on deep scans despite an estimated age of sixty thousand years.

The subsurface ocean harbors microbial life of genuine scientific interest, but it is the frozen vessel that drives research funding to Sorrow-Glacial. The sealed containers represent a potential biological windfall or an existential hazard, and the debate over whether to open them has divided the scientific community along lines that mirror the planet's own fracture zones.
